floor_history.headline: Recon: first C body landed (175->14 in one session); return-1 signature, mask intermediate, multi-set ptr LICM defeat, int-domain address order all confirmed; 4 residual classes mapped with dumps bank

Structural: floor 14 -> 10 (tail {+0,+0x65} store grouping = -2; a2 initialiser moved into the outer loop body = -2), and the reorg delay-slot residual's mechanism PROVEN with the instrumented cc1's B

frontier.hypothesis: Class D closes if a CODE_LABEL is materialised at the head of the inner-loop-2 if-body, making own_fallthrough==0 so reorg skips the fall-through steal and fills from the branch-target thread by copy+redirect (the target's shape, and the last insn of the count gap).
frontier.mechanism: reorg.c own_thread_p returns 0 on ANY CODE_LABEL between the branch and the thread's first active insn when label==NULL_RTX; with own_fallthrough==0 fill_eager_delay_slots' else-arm skips straight to the target-thread call. Option (b), an all-live mark_target_live_regs answer, needs find_basic_block()==-1 and is NOT C-reachable - do not spend probes on it.
frontier.next_probe: Try C shapes that put a label at the then-arm head: short-circuit `if (A || B)` respellings of the existing single bit test, and goto-into-the-arm shapes. Verify each BEFORE scoring by re-running tmp/grind/func_800770B8/s2/run_idump.sh with BB2_DBR_DEBUG=1 and reading the `own=` field of the `DBRDBG thr insn=<uid>` line for the inner-loop-2 beqz.

frontier.hypothesis: Class A(ii) - the ~3-row prologue cluster - is the ClearOTagR argument evaluation order: target emits the constant a1=0x1008 before the two-insn a0 global load, ours emits the a0 chain first because sched1 ranks its longer path to the jal higher.
frontier.mechanism: sched1 priority (longest path to the block end) beats LUID order in block 0; s2's H7 proved statement order DOES move block-0 insns, so the axis is live rather than a wall.
frontier.next_probe: Read tmp/grind/func_800770B8/s2/idumps/text1b.sched for block 0's computed priorities and ready-list order, then try argument-expression shapes that shorten the a0 chain or lengthen the a1 one (a named local read of the OT pointer before the call, a differently-typed OT argument). Re-measure the prologue register-save rows together with it - H7's regression came entirely from the save order, not from the addiu.

frontier.hypothesis: Classes B and C are register-allocator decisions with no remaining C spelling; they should be classified with the solver suite rather than probed with more source variants.
frontier.mechanism: B: our call-result temp dies at the copy into p_old (.lreg `Register 80 used 2 times`), and both directions of a second C handle collapse the build. C: rows 62-64 are a local-alloc dest-coalesce / reg_n_deaths decision - the row-pointer restructure (K3) and the int-domain address form (K5) both fail badly.
frontier.next_probe: Run tools/ra_solver inverse_compose.py classify on the p_old-vs-call-result seat (class B) and read .lreg's `dies in N places` for the row-62 base and offset pseudos behind the local-alloc-death-count gate (class C). Do NOT let this consume a session before frontier items 1 and 2 are spent.
